review.notes: The proposal is precise and reads like a natural change-impact request. Identifying the failing tests requires repository-specific reasoning about header normalization, framing, and connection behavior rather than a single lookup. The requested JSON list is clear. Although one accepted repair task concerns HEAD framing, this task investigates the broader impact of removing two categories of response-header rewriting and is not essentially the same investigation.

behavior_rationale.chunked_subcalls: The affected and unaffected cases span the long connection test module, I/O tests, and their helper semantics. Judging HTTP/1.0, HEAD, ordinary response completion, and error-response cases requires bounded semantic reads of more than one prompt-sized body of evidence.
behavior_rationale.combine_verify_finish: The deliverable is the union of failing test IDs from these investigations, which needs deduplication and validation against actual test definitions.
behavior_rationale.inspect_locate: The response-cleanup entry point must be connected to framing selection, writer installation, and tests using ConnectionPair rather than only tests calling the cleanup code directly.
behavior_rationale.recursive_decomposition: Impact can be investigated independently for HTTP/1.1 streaming responses, HTTP/1.0 and HEAD responses, explicit close handling, and spontaneous/error responses, then combined.

evidence.why: Implements both the framing-header rewrite and automatic Connection header handling being removed.
Determines which body adapter will be installed when the rewritten response lacks framing headers.
Explains why an unframed response no longer produces a serialized message terminator.
Contains independently affected persistence, streaming, HTTP/1.0, HEAD, pipelining, and error-response scenarios.
Direct writer tests help distinguish header serialization from Connection-level automatic rewriting.

spec.question: We are reviewing a proposal to reduce automatic response-header rewriting in Connection. For an unknown-length response, cleanup would still remove Content-Length and still remove Transfer-Encoding for an older or unknown peer. For an HTTP/1.1 peer, however, it would leave Transfer-Encoding exactly as supplied instead of setting it to chunked. Cleanup would also stop adding or rewriting Connection fields entirely, even when keep-alive has been disabled; any supplied Connection fields would remain untouched. All framing selection, state transitions, and writers would otherwise remain unchanged. Which existing tests would fail under this proposal? Return a JSON list of pytest node IDs.
